title: Generalizing the Denumerable Side of the ℵ₀/𝔠 Dichotomy
content: The parent entry proved that over any countably infinite commutative ring $R$ the univariate polynomial ring stays denumerable, $\#(R[X]) = \aleph_0$, while the full sequence space reaches the continuum, $\#(\mathbb{N} \to R) = \mathfrak{c}$. Its first open question asks whether the small side survives richer algebra. This file answers yes for two generalizations: countably many commuting variables (`MvPolynomial σ R`) and arbitrary monoid algebras (`MonoidAlgebra R M`). The header records the key structural insight — both are, by definition, finitely supported families over countable index sets, so countability is automatic and only the cardinality bookkeeping remains.

title: Countability via Doubly-Nested Finsupp
content: The crux of the multivariate case. By definition $\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R = \mathrm{AddMonoidAlgebra}\,R\,(\sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N}) = ((\sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N}) \to_0 R)$: a polynomial is a finitely supported map from monomials (themselves finitely supported exponent vectors $\sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N}$) to coefficients in $R$. Mathlib's `Finsupp.instCountable` says a Finsupp of countable types over a countable codomain is countable, and here it fires *twice* — first making the exponent space $\sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N}$ countable (from countable $\sigma$ and countable $\mathbb{N}$), then the coefficient family. The whole proof is a single `inferInstanceAs`, because the definitional unfolding lines up exactly with the instance.

title: Infinitude from the Constant Embedding
content: Infinitude is established the cheapest possible way: the constant-polynomial map $\mathrm{C} : R \to \mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R$ is injective (`MvPolynomial.C_injective`), so `Infinite.of_injective` transports `Infinite R` straight to the algebra. No monomials need to be counted — a single injected copy of the infinite ring $R$ suffices. Note this holds for *any* variable set $\sigma$, even empty, since the constant polynomials alone are already infinite.

title: Pinning the Cardinality at Exactly ℵ₀
content: With countability and infinitude in hand, `Cardinal.mk_eq_aleph0` collapses the cardinality to exactly $\aleph_0$ — a countable infinite type has cardinality precisely $\aleph_0$, neither finite nor continuum. `mk_mvPolynomial_eq_mk` then sharpens this to $\#(\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R) = \#R$: adjoining countably many commuting indeterminates produces a strictly larger ring but the same-size underlying set. This is the multivariate generalization of the parent's $\#(R[X]) = \aleph_0$.

title: Monoid Algebras: One Layer of Finsupp
content: The monoid-algebra case is the single-layer analogue. By definition $\mathrm{MonoidAlgebra}\,R\,M = (M \to_0 R)$ — finitely supported coefficient functions indexed by the monoid $M$. The same `Finsupp.instCountable` engine applies once. Notably, only the *type* structure of $M$ is used; no multiplicative or associativity hypotheses are required for countability, which is why the statement assumes merely `[Countable M]`.
mathContext: $\mathrm{MonoidAlgebra}\,R\,M = (M \to_0 R)$ is countable when $R$ and $M$ are.

title: Infinitude via a Single-Support Embedding
content: Infinitude here needs `[Nonempty M]`: fix a point $m_0 : M$, and the map $r \mapsto \mathrm{single}\,m_0\,r$ injects $R$ into $\mathrm{MonoidAlgebra}\,R\,M$. Injectivity is verified by evaluating at $m_0$ via `DFunLike.congr_fun ... m₀` and `Finsupp.single_eq_same` (which gives $(\mathrm{single}\,m_0\,r)\,m_0 = r$). This mirrors the constant embedding of the polynomial case — one injected coefficient line is enough.

title: Monoid-Algebra Cardinality is ℵ₀, Recovering ℚ[X]
content: Combining countability and infinitude, `mk_eq_aleph0` gives $\#(\mathrm{MonoidAlgebra}\,R\,M) = \aleph_0$, and `mk_monoidAlgebra_eq_mk` rewrites it as $\#R$. The conceptual payoff: setting $M = (\mathbb{N}, +)$ recovers $\mathrm{MonoidAlgebra}\,R\,\mathbb{N} = R[X]$, so the parent's univariate result is the special case of this theorem — the generalization is faithful, not a detour.

title: Concrete Instances over ℚ and ℤ
content: Three specializations make the abstract result tangible: $\#(\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,\mathbb{N}\,\mathbb{Q}) = \aleph_0$ (rational polynomials in countably many variables), $\#(\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,(\mathrm{Fin}\,3)\,\mathbb{Z}) = \aleph_0$ (integer polynomials in three variables), and $\#(\mathrm{MonoidAlgebra}\,\mathbb{Q}\,\mathbb{N}) = \aleph_0$ — the last being $\mathbb{Q}[X]$, closing the loop back to the parent. Each follows by typeclass inference alone, since $\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{N}, \mathrm{Fin}\,3$ all satisfy the countable/infinite/nonempty hypotheses automatically.
